title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: In most dinuclear lanthanide SMMs the slow relaxation is mainly single-ion in origin because radially contracted 4f orbitals give extraordinarily weak intramolecular exchange.
explanation: Section 2.3 generalizes that multinuclear Ln2 complexes, including common dinuclear Dy/Tb phthalocyanines, have weak intramolecular coupling, so the magnetic origin is predominantly a single-ion effect. The same shielding argument is repeated for clusters and polymers in Section 5.1, where weak coupling can still contribute to relaxation.
scope: Dinuclear and other multinuclear Ln complexes, especially Tb/Dy phthalocyanines.
caveats: Exceptions exist when a bridge enforces stronger coupling, as in the later bismuth-cluster-bridged Cp* Ln2Bi6 examples that show ferromagnetic blocking.
